ei.title: There’s More than One Way to Vote
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: We make many personal choices in our lives, from who to have lunch with to what career to pursue. However, there are many situations where we must make decisions as a group. Group decision-making is not as simple as our personal choices, as it involves numerous voices with differing opinions. Voting is often used to make group decisions fairer and more efficient, and various voting methods have been developed over time. The following story illustrates how these different voting methods work. The members of the Greenville High School student council needed to decide how to raise money for children in need. Their three options were an art show, a bake sale, and a charity concert, but there were conflicting opinions. So they decided to put it to a vote. When they asked for advice from Ms. Akers, the council’s advisor, she encouraged them not to use the familiar voting method, but to try something different instead. After doing some research, the council members decided to try three different voting systems: the first-past-the-post (FPTP) method, the alternative vote (AV) method, and the Condorcet method. The entire council was curious to find out if the different methods would yield different results. On the day of the vote, each possible event was given a letter: “art show” was represented by the letter A, the letter B indicated “bake sale,” and C stood for “charity concert.” Each of the 20 council members was given a voting slip and instructed to write down the options in order of preference. For example, if the charity concert was their first choice, followed by the bake sale and the art show, they would write CBA. After every member had voted, the voting slips were counted. The results were as follows: The First-Past-The-Post Method The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods. Voters are given several options, and whichever gets the most first-preference votes wins. Neither the second nor third preference matters at all, so they are ignored. This method is commonly used in political elections around the world. The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert. This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7. The FPTP method is uncomplicated and easy to understand, but it has a significant weakness. It is possible to win a vote without the support of the majority. That was the case here. According to the results of the FPTP method, the council’s choice was to hold a charity concert. However, only 8 out of 20 council members chose the charity concert as their first preference, which equaled 40% of the total votes. The Alternative Vote Method Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. The AV method can potentially include more than one round of counting. For an option to win in the first round, it needs to get more than 50% of the first-preference votes. As the charity concert only received 40% of the total votes, a second round of counting was required. Option A, the art show, received the fewest first-preference votes, with only 5 council members voting for it. Therefore, option A was eliminated, and the 5 council members’ votes were redistributed based on their second preferences. As a result, 4 votes for option B (ABC) and 1 for option C (ACB) were added to the total. This meant that option B had 11 total votes, while option C had only 9. As a result, the bake sale would be the winner. Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either. It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes. In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received. The Condorcet Method Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method. This method involves comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options. In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs. B, B vs. C, and A vs. C. Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB. Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA. Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9. They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9. As option A, the art show, was preferred to both of the other options, it would be considered the winner. The Condorcet method’s weakness is that, along with being complex, it sometimes fails to select a winner. This is especially true in elections that contain numerous options. It is possible that no option will be clearly preferred over the others. Instead of all methods pointing toward a single option and making the council’s choice easier, the winner differed with each method. After a long, intense discussion with Ms. Akers, the student council members decided to choose the Condorcet method, as they liked the idea of directly comparing each option with the others. Everyone agreed that they learned a lot about different voting systems through this experience. It is obvious that choosing an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task. No voting system is flawless or clearly superior to another. Whichever we choose will have pros and cons. Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not ranking our choices at all. Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, arguing that more complex methods deliver more accurate results. All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make better decisions as a society. Ultimately, understanding all of the possible voting methods and weighing their pros and cons allows us to better understand the process of decision-making. When we understand decision-making better, we are more likely to become better decision-makers ourselves.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② instructing → instructed: 'was given ... and (was) instructed'로 이어지는 병렬 수동태이므로 과거분사 instructed
det.analysis:
① given: 'Each of the 20 council members was given a voting slip'에서 각 구성원이 투표용지를 '받은' 것이라 수동태 과거분사 given이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② instructing → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'was given a voting slip and ___ to write down the options'는 'was given ...'과 'was instructed ...'가 and로 나란히 이어지는 구조예요. 앞이 수동태(was given)이므로 뒤도 똑같이 과거분사 instructed(지시받은)로 맞춰야 해요. instructing으로 쓰면 병렬이 깨져 틀려요. ❌ instructing은 틀림 ←정답

③ followed: 'followed by the bake sale'는 '빵 판매가 그 뒤를 잇는' 수동의 뜻이라 과거분사 followed가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ counted: 'the voting slips were counted'에서 투표용지가 '집계된' 것이라 수동태 counted가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: A and B 병렬: 앞이 수동태(was given)면 뒤도 수동태(was instructed)로

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① what → which: 앞 문장 전체(내용)를 받아 콤마 뒤에서 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법이므로 which
det.analysis:
① what → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! '~ chose the charity concert as their first preference, ___ equaled 40% of the total votes'에서 콤마 뒤의 관계사는 앞 문장 전체(8명이 자선 콘서트를 골랐다는 사실)를 받아 '그리고 그것은 40%에 해당했다'로 이어 주는 계속적 용법이에요. 이때는 which를 써야 하고, what은 앞의 내용을 받을 수 없어 틀려요. ❌ what은 틀림 ←정답

② required: 'a second round of counting was required'에서 2차 집계가 '요구된' 것이라 수동태 required가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ eliminated: 'option A was eliminated'에서 A안이 '탈락된' 것이라 수동태 eliminated가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ redistributed: 'the votes were redistributed'에서 표가 '재분배된' 것이라 수동태 redistributed가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 콤마 뒤에서 앞 문장 전체를 받는 계속적 용법 → which (what 불가)

questions.passage: It is obvious that ①<u>choosing</u> an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task.  No voting system is flawless or clearly superior to another.  Whichever we choose will have pros and cons.  Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not ranking our choices at all.  Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, ②<u>argued</u> that more complex methods deliver more accurate results.  All of these efforts are ③<u>designed</u> not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make better decisions as a society.  Ultimately, ④<u>understanding</u> all of the possible voting methods and weighing their pros and cons allows us to better understand the process of decision-making.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② argued → arguing: 접속사 없이 앞 절에 이어지는 분사구문이므로 현재분사 arguing
det.analysis:
① choosing: 'choosing an ideal voting method is a complex ... task'에서 '~을 고르는 것'이 문장의 주어라 동명사 choosing이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② argued → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, ___ that more complex methods deliver more accurate results'에서 콤마 뒤는 접속사 없이 앞 절에 이어지는 분사구문이에요. '~라고 주장하면서'라는 능동의 뜻이므로 현재분사 arguing으로 써야 해요. argued(과거동사)를 쓰면 접속사 없이 동사가 둘이 되어 틀려요. ❌ argued는 틀림 ←정답

③ designed: 'All of these efforts are designed not to make ~'에서 노력들이 '설계된' 것이라 수동태 designed가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ understanding: 'understanding all of the possible voting methods and weighing ~ allows us to ~'에서 '~을 이해하는 것'이 문장의 주어라 동명사 understanding이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 콤마 뒤 접속사 없이 이어지는 분사구문은 현재분사(-ing): arguing(주장하면서)

questions.passage: The entire council was ①<u>curious</u> to find out if the different methods would yield different results.  On the day of the vote, each possible event was given a letter: “art show” was represented by the letter A, the letter B indicated “bake sale,” and C stood for “charity concert. ” Each of the 20 council members was given a voting ②<u>slip</u> and instructed to write down the options in order of ③<u>confusion</u>.  For example, if the charity concert was their first choice, followed by the bake sale and the art show, they would write CBA.  After every member had voted, the voting slips were counted.  The results were as follows: The First-Past-The-Post Method The FPTP method is the ④<u>simplest</u> of the three methods.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ confusion → preference: 선호(preference)하는 순서대로 선택지를 적으라고 지시함
det.analysis:
① curious: 학생회 전체가 방식마다 결과가 다를지 '궁금해했다'는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

② slip: 각 구성원에게 투표'용지(voting slip)'가 주어졌다는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

③ confusion → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'write down the options in order of preference'로 '선호하는 순서대로 선택지를 적으라'는 뜻이에요. 투표에서 순위를 매기는 것이므로 preference(선호)가 맞는데, confusion(혼란)은 문맥에 전혀 맞지 않아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

④ simplest: FPTP가 세 방식 중 '가장 단순한' 방식이라는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: in order of preference(선호 순서대로) — 순위를 매겨 적는 것이라 preference

questions.passage: It is ①<u>obvious</u> that choosing an ideal voting method is a complex and challenging task.  No voting system is ②<u>flawless</u> or clearly superior to another.  Whichever we choose will have ③<u>pros</u> and cons.  Some people believe that it is best to keep the process simple by not ranking our choices at all.  Others continue to develop and test new ways of voting, arguing that more complex methods deliver more ④<u>confusing</u> results.  All of these efforts are designed not to make decision-making difficult and inefficient, but to help us make better decisions as a society.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ confusing → accurate: 더 복잡한 방식이 더 '정확한(accurate)' 결과를 낸다고 주장함
det.analysis:
① obvious: 이상적 투표 방식을 고르는 일이 복잡하고 까다롭다는 것이 '분명하다'는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

② flawless: 어떤 투표 제도도 '흠이 없거나' 명백히 우월하지 않다는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

③ pros: 어떤 것을 고르든 '장점(pros)'과 단점이 있다는 문맥에 적절해요. ✅ 적절

④ confusing → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'more complex methods deliver more accurate results'로, 더 복잡한 방식이 더 '정확한(accurate)' 결과를 낸다고 주장하는 사람들의 근거예요. 복잡한 방식을 옹호하는 흐름이라 accurate가 맞는데, confusing(혼란스러운)은 그 주장과 반대라 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 복잡한 방식을 옹호하는 근거 → more accurate results(더 정확한 결과), confusing 아님

questions.passage: The results were as follows: The First-Past-The-Post Method The FPTP method is the simplest of the three methods.  Voters are given several options, and whichever gets __________ wins.  Neither the second nor third preference matters at all, so they are ignored.  This method is commonly used in political elections around the world.  The student council quickly determined that the winner would be option C, the charity concert.  This was because it received 8 first-preference votes, while option A received 5 and option B received 7.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① the most first-preference votes(가장 많은 1순위 표): FPTP는 1순위 최다 득표가 이김
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'Voters are given several options, and whichever gets ___ wins.'(유권자에게 여러 선택지가 주어지고, ___을 얻은 쪽이 이긴다). 바로 뒤 문장에서 '2·3순위는 전혀 중요하지 않다'고 했으므로, 이기는 기준은 '가장 많은 1순위 표'예요.

✅ ① the most first-preference votes(가장 많은 1순위 표): 뒤 문장(2·3순위 무시)과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ② the fewest possible votes(가능한 가장 적은 표): 최다 득표가 이긴다는 설명과 반대예요.

❌ ③ the advisor's final approval(조언자의 최종 승인): 조언자가 승자를 정하는 게 아니에요.

❌ ④ an equal number of votes(동일한 수의 표): FPTP의 승리 기준과 무관해요.
det.tip: 2·3순위는 무시(ignored) → 1순위 최다 득표(the most first-preference votes)가 승리 기준

questions.passage: Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9.  In other words, 11 people preferred A to B, voting either ABC, ACB, or CAB.  Meanwhile, 9 people preferred B to A by voting BAC, BCA, or CBA.  Interestingly, the voters preferred option B to option C by the same count of 11 to 9.  They also preferred option A to option C by 11 to 9.  As option A, the art show, was __________, it would be considered the winner.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ preferred to both of the other options(다른 두 선택지보다 모두 선호된): 그래서 A가 승자로 여겨짐
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'As option A, the art show, was ___, it would be considered the winner.'(A안(예술 전시회)이 ___했기 때문에, 그것이 승자로 여겨질 것이었다). 앞에서 A가 B보다, 또 A가 C보다 11대 9로 선호되었다고 했으므로, A는 '다른 두 선택지보다 모두 선호된' 것이에요.

❌ ① counted more than once(한 번 넘게 집계된): Condorcet 방식의 '쌍대 비교' 결과와 맞지 않아요.

❌ ② rejected by the members(구성원들에게 거부된): A가 승자로 여겨진 흐름과 반대예요.

✅ ③ preferred to both of the other options(다른 두 선택지보다 모두 선호된): A가 B·C 둘 다에 앞섰다는 앞 내용과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ④ given the fewest votes(가장 적은 표를 받은): A가 승자가 된 상황과 반대예요.
det.tip: A가 B에도, C에도 앞섬 → preferred to both of the other options(다른 두 선택지보다 모두 선호됨)

ch: preferred to both of the other options

questions.passage: Unfortunately, the AV method is not perfect either.  It sometimes allows second-preference votes to have a greater influence than first-preference votes.  In this case, the bake sale won, but this was mainly due to the second-preference votes it received.  The Condorcet Method Finally, the student council counted the votes using the Condorcet method.  This method involves comparing the voters’ preferences between each possible pair of options.  In this case, there were three pairs to consider: A vs.  B, B vs.  C, and A vs.  C.  Through this method, the student council discovered that its members preferred option A to option B by a count of 11 to 9. questions.passage: The Alternative Vote Method Next, the council members examined the votes using the AV method, and they soon realized that there would be a different result. det.korean: This method is commonly used in political elections around the world
det.analysis:
'이 방식은 흔히 사용된다'는 '~되다'라는 수동의 뜻이라 수동태(be + 과거분사)로 써요.

주어는 This method(이 방식)이고, 동사는 'is + used'(사용된다)예요. 빈도부사 commonly(흔히)는 be동사와 과거분사 사이에 넣어요: This + method + is + commonly + used.

'정치 선거에서'는 in political elections로 써요: in + political + elections.

'전 세계의'는 around the world로 마무리해요: around + the + world.

순서대로 이으면 This / method / is / commonly / used / in / political / elections / around / the / world.
det.tip: 수동태 is used + 빈도부사 commonly는 be동사 뒤에: is commonly used(흔히 사용되다)
